news.title: How the vineyard by the lake is changing Batu's economy
news.summary: The Reporter visits Castel's vineyard, set up in Batu in 2007, and finds steady jobs, new skills for young workers and new hotels and restaurants along the shore.
news.body: A feature in The Reporter describes how Castel, the French wine group that planted its vineyard by Lake Dambal in 2007, has become part of daily life in Batu. Local workers describe steady wages and training in modern farming. The article notes new asphalt roads, boutique hotels and lakeside restaurants serving visitors from Addis Ababa and abroad, and links the town's growth to Ethiopia's wider economic opening.

news.title: Researchers map ten tourist sites around Batu
news.summary: A new study used GIS to map 17 tourist sites around Bishoftu and Batu, ten of them in the Batu area, with descriptions in Afaan Oromoo, Amharic and English.
news.body: Researchers mapped tourist sites within 35 km of Bishoftu and Batu, recording GPS points, photographs and descriptions in three languages. Ten of the 17 sites are in and around Batu. The dataset also includes hotels, health centres, banks, police stations and fuel stations, so that visitors can plan trips with the services they need. The city plans to use this kind of data in the Discover Batu map.

news.title: Thousands celebrate Timket on Lake Dambal
news.summary: Tabots crossed the lake by boat and thousands of faithful gathered on the shore and on the water for Timket, photographed by AP and the BBC.
news.body: Ethiopian Orthodox faithful celebrated Timket on Lake Dambal on 18 and 19 January 2026. Priests carried tabots from the churches to the lake shore with chants, crosses and ceremonial umbrellas, and boats circled on the water. At dawn the priests blessed the lake and sprinkled the crowd. International media, including the Associated Press and the BBC, published photographs from Batu, and visitors came from Addis Ababa and abroad.

news.title: Batu prepares to celebrate Timket on the natural lake
news.summary: Church leaders said tabots would be blessed on up to four islands and carried across the lake by boat to Bocceessaa, with six churches gathering for the ceremony.
news.body: Liqe Tiguhan Aleqa Ermiyas H/Giorgis of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church in Batu told AMN that the city's Timket is special because it is held on a natural lake. Tabots are received on up to four islands, placed on boats and carried across the lake to Bocceessaa, where six churches gather. He thanked residents of other faiths for helping clean the city and prepare the event, and said the city administration had set up committees to make the celebration a success.

news.title: Ardaa Jilaa Qixxee Waayyuu reopens after 63 years
news.summary: The Gadaa ceremonial ground north of the city, beside Lake Dambal, has reopened. It is where the Oromo of the Batu area made laws and held blessings.
news.body: The Culture and Tourism Office announced that Ardaa Jilaa Qixxee Waayyuu, closed for more than 63 years, has reopened. Office head Kamaal Badhaasoo said the site, in Malkaa Shaalloo kebele near the lake, was where the Oromo people of the area made their laws, gathered in hard times and received guidance. Abbaa Gadaa Abdurrahimaan Dhaqqabii described it as a place of prayer and assembly, and said earlier governments had taken it from the community. The office says the site also has strong potential for tourism.

news.title: Corridor development under way in 34 Oromia cities
news.summary: The Oromia Urban and Housing Development Bureau says corridor projects are running in 34 of the region's higher-grade cities, alongside greening and urban agriculture.
news.body: The head of the Oromia Urban and Housing Development Bureau, Mahammad Guuyyee, said corridor development is under way in 34 higher-grade cities in Oromia, with each city working to its own potential. The programme combines roads, public spaces, greening and urban agriculture. In Batu, corridor work includes the lakeside development and new road links such as the corridor from the OSU roundabout to the TVET College.

news.title: Tourism income passes 1.1 billion birr
news.summary: Mayor Ahmedin Ismail reported tourism income rising from 300 million birr in 2023 to 654 million in 2024 and over 1.1 billion this fiscal year, with a target of 1.8 billion next year.
news.body: The mayor said corridor development, the Lake Batu development project, new standard hotels and resorts, and peace and security have driven the growth. The city has become a destination for conferences as well as leisure, and the annual Timket on the lake draws more domestic and international visitors every year. The target for the next fiscal year is more than 1.8 billion birr.

news.title: Oromia State University hosts international research symposium
news.summary: The 2nd International and 12th National Research Symposium, on smart public service delivery through digital platforms, was held at the OSU main campus in Batu.
news.body: Oromia State University, founded in 2009 and based in Batu, hosted its 2nd International and 12th National Research Symposium under the theme 'Smart Public Service Delivery through Digital Platforms and Innovation'. Guests included leaders of the University of Juba in South Sudan.

news.title: Lake partners meet in Batu to plan water protection
news.summary: Technical committees of the Dembel-Shalla Sub-Basin platform met in Batu to plan water monitoring, pollution control and watershed work for 2025.
news.body: About 50 public, private and civil society partners formed the Dembel-Shalla Sub-Basin Multi-Stakeholder Platform in 2024. From 25 to 27 March 2025 its three technical committees met in Batu for the first time. They agreed to promote a water-use monitoring system, raise water-use efficiency in farming, support water-quality and wetland monitoring, give guidance on wastewater, and map erosion hotspots in the sub-basin.
